description:
Estimates year-one federal + state tax savings from operating a property as a short-term rental, leveraging the 'STR loophole' (cost segregation + bonus depreciation + active-income offset when material participation requirements are met).

Returns: `status` (`qualifies` | `does_not_qualify` | `needs_review`), `statusLabel` (show this to the user: "May qualify" | "Does not qualify" | "Needs review"; it's an estimate, never a guarantee) and `reasons` (one entry per test: `code`, `severity`, plain-English `message`, `learnMore` code section — show the messages to the user, they explain WHY), `firstYearSavings` (the savings the user actually gets in year one — the active-income offset only when the loophole applies, otherwise the passive treatment, which is usually $0 with no other passive income), `potentialSavingsIfQualified` (the active-offset figure if they did qualify), `qualifies` (boolean, true only when `status` is `qualifies`; kept for compatibility), `bonusDepreciation`, `totalDepreciation`, `paperLoss`, `combinedMarginalRate`, `passiveCarryforward` (0 when the loss is non-passive), `excessOverEblThreshold` (§461(l), when the limit is known), `disclaimer`, plus any `warnings` the calculator surfaced, and echoed inputs (`marginalBracketPct`, `propertyPrice`, `yearPlacedInService`).

The estimator uses standard cost-segregation component ratios (20% personal property / 10% land improvements / 70% structure) and current bonus depreciation rates by year placed in service. Operating numbers (revenue, opex, mortgage interest) are derived from typical STR heuristics — 8% gross revenue / 40% opex ratio / 75% LTV / 7.5% rate / 30y term — so the caller only needs to provide the purchase price and tax profile. This is an underwriting illustration, NOT a substitute for a cost-segregation study or CPA advice. **Always tell the user to consult a CPA before relying on this.**

Use this tool when the user wants to understand the after-tax cash impact of buying a property as an STR, is evaluating whether the STR loophole applies, or is comparing acquisition tax outcomes across price points.

Required: `purchase_price`, `year_placed_in_service` (2025, 2026, or 2027), `marginal_tax_bracket` (one of 0.22, 0.24, 0.32, 0.35, 0.37), `avg_guest_stay_days` (decimals allowed; 7 or less can qualify, 8–30 needs review for significant personal services, over 30 is a rental activity), `materially_participates` (boolean — true only if the user will spend 100+ hours/year managing AND that's not less than anyone else (including cleaners, co-hosts and property managers); ask the user to confirm before assuming true). Optional: `state_marginal_rate` (default 0), `land_value_percent` (default 0.20), `participation_hours` + `others_max_hours` + `others_total_hours` (evaluate the hour tests instead of trusting the flag), `personal_use_days` + `rental_days` (§280A), `filing_status` (§461(l)), `state` (bonus conformity). Not tax advice.

No STRvest account needed. To save results or run full underwriting, the user can create a free account at https://strvest.com/sign-up and connect the authenticated STRvest MCP server (https://strvest.com/mcp).

avg_guest_stay_days.description: Average period of customer use in days (total rental days ÷ number of stays; decimals allowed). 7 or less can qualify; over 7 and up to 30 needs review (may still qualify if significant personal services are provided); over 30 is a rental activity. Typical STR averages 3-5 days.

filing_status.description: Optional. Filing status, for the §461(l) excess business loss check. Default single.

land_value_percent.description: Optional. Land's share of total purchase price as a decimal — depreciable basis = purchase price × (1 − this). Default 0.20 reflects typical suburban single-family. Lower for condos / land-light properties, higher for primarily-land properties.

marginal_tax_bracket.description: User's federal marginal income tax bracket as a decimal (NOT a percent). Allowed values: 0.22, 0.24, 0.32, 0.35, 0.37. If the user gives you a percent (e.g. '32%'), convert to 0.32. Ask the user what bracket they're in — don't guess.

materially_participates.description: Whether the user will materially participate in the rental business. IRS test: 100+ hours per year AND not less than anyone else (including cleaners, co-hosts and property managers), OR 500+ hours total. Required for the loophole to convert paper loss into an active-income offset. If the user has a property manager doing most of the work, this is false. Ask before assuming true.

others_max_hours.description: Optional. Most hours put in by any single other person (cleaner, co-host, property manager). Needed for the 100-hour test.

others_total_hours.description: Optional. All other people's hours combined. 0 means the owner did all the work (substantially-all test).

participation_hours.description: Optional. Hours the owner (and spouse) spent on the rental this year. When given, the material participation tests (500 hours / substantially all / 100 hours and not less than anyone else) are evaluated from hours instead of the materially_participates flag.

personal_use_days.description: Optional. Days of personal use by the owner/family this year (default 0). Over the greater of 14 days or 10% of rental days, the home may be a residence under §280A and losses may be limited.

purchase_price.description: Property purchase price in US dollars. REQUIRED. Example: 850000 for $850,000.

rental_days.description: Optional. Days rented at fair rental this year (for the §280A personal-use test).

state.description: Optional. Two-letter state code, for the state bonus-depreciation conformity check.

state_marginal_rate.description: Optional. State marginal income tax rate as a decimal (not a percent). Defaults to 0 (federal-only display).

year_placed_in_service.description: Calendar year the property will first be rented as an STR. Only 2025, 2026, and 2027 are supported — bonus depreciation rates change by year.
